input.brief: Hardev Mobile Communication, Bareilly: 19-year-old cell phone repair shop — Samsung, Vivo, Xiaomi, OnePlus, Apple, Oppo, Realme; screen replacement, buttons, charger ports, network problems, unlocking; most repairs same day

direction.name: One motif
direction.idea: Take one shape from the subject and let it run the whole system. A drilling tool's octagonal cross-section becomes the buttons, the image masks and the loader. A two-account money app becomes two circles that recur as icon, inline dot and section colour. A café's striped awning becomes every band on the page. Look at the product, the logo, the object or the word in the headline and find the simplest geometry in it (a circle, an arc, a chamfer, a stripe, a notch, a ring). Then use only that shape, at three or four very different scales, everywhere a designer would normally reach for a generic rounded rectangle.
direction.composition: Hero: the motif appears once at enormous scale as a flat filled shape, cropped by the viewport (a circle 120vh across entering from the right, a chamfered block filling the lower half), with a short headline at 6–8vw and one supporting sentence set on the remaining ground, left-aligned on a shared margin. Through the page the motif returns as: the mask for every photograph (via `clip-path` or `border-radius` made from the same geometry), the shape of the primary button, the bullet beside list items at text size, and one full-width band that separates the two halves of the page. Sections use simple two-column or single-column layouts so the shape is the only thing with character.
direction.typography: A clean geometric or grotesk face that echoes the shape (round bowls for circles, squared terminals for chamfers). Medium weight; headings 6–8vw in the hero and 3–4vw after.
direction.colour: The motif carries the accent colour at large scale, flat. Everything else is ground and ink. A second motif colour is allowed only if the subject has a real pair (two accounts, two modes).
direction.imagery: Photographs appear inside the motif's shape. If there is product interface to show, it sits on a flat colour stage shaped by the motif. Draw the shape with CSS or a simple inline SVG path; do not draw illustrations.
direction.richness: One shape at many sizes. The giant cropped shape gives the hero mass and colour without a single image.
direction.pitfalls: One motif means one. A circle here, a hexagon there and a blob behind is the generated look this replaces. The motif must come from the subject and you must be able to say from where in one clause.

hero.name: Striped card beside the room
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split 50/50 with a 12px gap and 12px outer margins. The right half is one full-height photograph of the room, corners radiused 16px, `position: sticky` so it stays in view while the left half scrolls. The left half is a printed card: a flat paper-colour panel with the same 16px radius, and the subject's stripe (from its awning, label or ribbon) as the only ornament. Across the card's top runs a band 56px tall made of alternating bars of the single ink colour and paper, each bar 28px wide, built as a flex row of filled blocks. The same stripe returns as an 8px band above the footer and inside the button on hover. Under the band, centred: the wordmark about 300px wide, then a two-line headline in a light serif at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px) in the ink colour, one supporting sentence at 17px held to 36ch, and the single action as a solid rectangular button. Three text links sit in one centred row at 15px, 28px above the card's bottom edge. One ink on paper; the photograph supplies every other colour.
hero.mobile: The photograph comes first at full width inside 12px margins, 48svh tall, with the 16px radius. The card follows and overlaps the photograph's bottom edge by 24px using a negative margin. Its striped band is 40px tall; below it the wordmark at 56% width, the headline at 8vw on two lines, the sentence and the button, all centred. The links wrap into the card's foot.
hero.headline: A warm two-line welcome of three to six words, up to about 18 characters per line at 3.6vw.

type.name: Bricolage Grotesque

display.settings: weight 600 · tracking -0.04em · leading 0.92 · sentence case; leave optical sizing on so large sizes tighten and gain contrast
display.css:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bricolage+Grotesque:wght@400;500;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">

type.note: A grotesk with visible stroke contrast and slightly irregular curves, so headings look drawn rather than engineered. Suits reports, consultancies and design-led software that want warmth without a serif.

palette.name: Greys and mint
palette.note: White, near-black and two greys fill a board of flat tiles. Mint floods a few whole tiles (one statement, one figure, the closing call to action) and appears nowhere else.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Statement with inline thumbnails
sections.blueprint: A centred statement of 18–28 words, four lines at clamp(32px, 4.2vw, 62px), medium or bold weight, leading 1.12, in a block 60–66% of the viewport wide with 22vh of empty ground above and below. Three to five small frames sit inline between words: each is an `inline-block` 0.85em tall and 0.85–1.3em wide, `vertical-align: -0.1em`, radius 0.14em, holding a tightly cropped photograph (or a crop of real interface) of the thing the neighbouring word names. Frames are part of the line, never floating over it, with 0.12em of space either side. No heading above and no paragraph below; the statement is set as a `p`. Directly under the section the page may split into two flat colour halves or begin the first product row, so the thumbnails read as a preview of what follows. On a motif-driven page every frame takes the motif's shape.
sections.mobile: Left-aligned instead of centred, at 8vw with leading 1.15, about seven lines inside 20px margins. Keep at most three inline frames, each exactly one cap-height tall, and make sure none lands at the start of a line. Vertical padding drops to 96px.

sections.name: Specimens on colour tiles
sections.blueprint: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
sections.mobile: The heading and its sentence sit on top at full width. Tiles become a two-column grid with 8px gaps; the double tile spans both columns at 8:5 and comes first. Names shrink to 17px and facts to 15px, still under each tile.

sections.name: Square plate, spare text
sections.blueprint: One flat field split 50/50, at least 88svh tall. Left half: a single square photograph filling the half's width minus 40px margins, vertically centred, square corners. A large simple shape may be laid over it to turn the photograph into the object it stands for: a ring 86% of its width with a 6px stroke and a small solid dot at the centre makes a record; a notch cut by clip-path makes a ticket stub. Right half, a flex column with space-between: at the top a row of three plain text tabs at 18px (editions, years, variants), the active one in full ink and the others at 40%; in the middle the title, two to four words at 32–40px bold, with a 34ch description 48px below; along the bottom two filled rectangular cells side by side, each half the column wide and 72px tall, acting as the two actions, one in ink and one a tone off the field.
sections.mobile: The square photograph comes first at full width with 16px margins. The tabs sit under it as one row at 17px. Then the title at 28px, the description, and the two action cells stacked, each full width and 60px tall.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: The mark, built large
sections.blueprint: On a flat colour field, the brand closes the page as a construction rather than as set type. Across the full content width and about 34svh tall, the wordmark is built from blocks: each letter is knocked out of its own solid rectangle in a palette colour, the rectangles differ in height (60–100% of the band) and butt together with 4px gaps, bottoms on one line. Where the project has a simple geometric mark or motif, enlarge that instead, drawn as inline SVG from flat rectangles, circles and quarter-arcs with the same 4px gaps. Below, 56px lower: four columns of plain links at 15px across columns 1–8, and two addresses or contact lines in columns 9–12. A last row carries the copyright at the left and one small filled button at the right. Space and the block construction do all the separating.
sections.mobile: The block wordmark spans the full width at about 22svh tall; a long name breaks into two rows of blocks. Link columns go two across at 15px, contact lines beneath at full width, then copyright and the small button on one row.

references.name: Superlocal 2026
references.idea: Everything is a circle: a dot-matrix logotype whose dots become floating photo circles and glowing orbs across a grey-to-orange field.
references.hero: Mid-grey field with a faint dot grid (one dot every 33px) that fades through the lower half into saturated orange at the bottom edge. The captured first paint contains one element: a 270×80px logotype dead centre, built from black ellipses of varying size, its letters progressively compressed to the right. No nav or text yet. After loading, a cluster of four small pills (one black, three white) appears top-centre; the logo turns white inside a 330px ring of about fifty tiny circles — round photo crops, glowing orbs, coins; and the bottom edge carries the event name left and dates right in an outlined dot-matrix face 40px tall.
references.type: Display text is an outlined dot-matrix face drawn on canvas, about 40px caps, modules flickering. All other text is one tight bold grotesk ('fontSans') from 12 to 24px with negative tracking. The logotype is built from ellipses on the same matrix.
references.colour: #bcbcbc #ff641e #1a1302 #ffb740 #c13bff #ffffff — Every screen repeats a vertical fade from flat grey to hot orange. Orbs add magenta-violet cores; the footer swaps to a soft yellow glow. Text is near-black, nav pills black and white.
references.imagery: Event photographs cropped to circles from 60 to 240px, floating without a grid alongside hard-edged radial-gradient orbs and coin images; some pairs overlap. The logo and footer art are generated dot matrices.
references.layout: No visible grid: circles drift across each screen while text locks to the bottom corners (statement bottom-left, description bottom-right). A four-pill nav stays top-centre. The footer resolves into three text columns over a screen-filling dot-matrix glow.

sections.description: No grid. Circular photo crops between 60 and 240px across float over the grey-to-orange field, a few overlapping in pairs. A flat radial orb (orange rim, magenta-violet core, about 160px) sits among them and others are cut by the viewport edges. The pill nav stays top-centre; nothing else is fixed.

Bottom-left: a small bold date line, then a two-line statement in the outlined dot-matrix face at about 36px, some modules lit orange mid-animation. Bottom-right: a two-line 12px bold description. Above them three photo circles (190px portrait near centre, poster collage left, stage shot right) and a large orb top-right.

Grey field with a huge soft yellow radial glow. The dot-matrix logo is enlarged to fill the screen, its ellipses knocked out of the yellow in grey. On top: three columns of bold 18px text (contact message and email left, press list centre, socials right), a tiny credits list, and a bottom line with dates, year and city in the same three columns.

steal: Build the logotype from a dot matrix of ellipses of varying size, then reuse the same matrix at screen-filling scale as the footer background.
Crop every photo to a circle at wildly different diameters and let them float with coloured orbs instead of sitting in a gallery grid.
Fade each screen from flat grey into one saturated colour at its bottom edge so the viewport itself carries the brand colour.

references.name: Tara
references.idea: Two pastel circles, mint for saving and pink for spending, stand for the app's two accounts and recur as icon, inline dot, section colour and card gradient.
references.hero: Off-white field with no navigation, only a small bold wordmark top-left. The left column is vertically centred and starts about 8% in: a two-line headline in a wide heavy grotesk at roughly 6vw with tight leading, a grey one-line subhead beneath, then a pill-shaped email field about 400px wide with a black pill button nested inside its right end. The right half holds a 3D pair floating on the page colour: a mint-to-pink gradient bank card tilted about 30 degrees, overlapping a perspective-tilted phone showing a balance screen. Two small award badges are stacked on the right edge. Roughly half the viewport is empty.
references.type: Herokid Wide at weight 600 with -0.04em tracking for headlines, regular-width Herokid for everything else. Sentence case in the hero, all-caps for the scroll statements. Roughly 86px headline against 14px body, with a mid size of about 24px for centred explainer lines.
references.colour: #f8f8f8 #0a0a0a #c3edce #f8c7c9 #ffffff — Near-white base with black type. Mint and pink appear only as the two account colours: first as small circles, then as full-screen section fields and a soft glow behind the footer wordmark.
references.imagery: 3D bank card and tilted phone mock-ups carrying app screens, floating without a container on the page colour; later a straight-on phone on a flat mint field. Simple line icons inside solid pastel circles.
references.layout: Twenty screens of scroll but very little per screen: one centred object or statement per viewport with large empty margins. A wordmark top-left and a tiny pill button top-right persist. Full-bleed pastel fields mark the two product chapters; a row of four white cards closes.

sections.description: A pinned, nearly empty viewport where a single mint circle holding a line icon sits upper-centre with a pink circle peeking from behind it. On scroll the pink circle slides out to sit beside the mint one, overlapping slightly, each with its own icon, and three centred lines of roughly 24px text appear beneath explaining the two accounts. Nothing else is on screen.

A chapter-title screen: two words of heavy uppercase at about 5vw, centred and stacked on two lines, with a mint dot the height of the capitals sitting inline after the first word like punctuation. The dot is the same circle from the previous scene, so the colour carries its meaning straight into the full-mint section that follows.

Full-viewport mint field. A small eyebrow and a bold product name are centred near the top. Below, a straight-on phone mock-up stands just right of centre, and a short right-aligned bold claim with two lines of small text sits to its left, level with the phone's lower third. Text and phone hug the centre line, leaving both outer thirds empty.

After four white rounded cards and a repeated centred email pill, the footer is one row of small links and then the wordmark set enormous, around 45vw wide and cropped by the bottom edge. It is white on the off-white page and becomes visible only through blurred pink and mint glows placed behind the letters.

steal: Assign each product concept a colour and a shape early (two pastel circles), then reuse it as bullet, inline punctuation dot and full section background.
Nest the call-to-action button inside the email field's pill so the form reads as one object.
Set the footer wordmark in the page's own background colour and reveal it only with soft coloured glows behind the letters.

references.name: BEIGE FORCE
references.idea: A game's cast presented as a bitmap type specimen: black pixel glyphs in a ruled grid on a mustard field, each given a blandly fashionable first name.
references.hero: Flat mustard yellow with fine grain fills the viewport. A one-line mono header spans the width with 28px margins: credit left, title flanked by lightning glyphs centre, a quote and a help link right, with a black hairline under it. Two 14px mono text columns start at the second of four grid columns; a pixel-font PLAY! button with a white-and-black double border sits in the fourth. From one third down, a four-column grid of square hairline-bordered cells fills the width, each holding one large black pixel glyph and a small centred name. A narrow strip on the right edge shows the game's blue and magenta screen.
references.type: Monaspace Neon mono at 14px for every word of text, regular and bold only; Kongtext bitmap face at 36px for the button and the mobile lock-out heading. The real display type is the grid of hand-built pixel glyphs roughly 190px tall.
references.colour: #e1ac10 #0b0b0b #2c3e9e #e6157f #4a97db — One warm mustard field with black ink only. A sliver of royal blue and hot magenta at the right edge hints at the game, and the mobile lock-out screen flips to flat sky blue.
references.imagery: Pixel-art icons and letters (sailboat, saucer, insect, building, capitals, punctuation) drawn as black squares with visible gaps between pixels, one per cell, centred. No photographs.
references.layout: A fixed frame: header rule, intro band, then a strict four-column grid of equal square cells that scrolls inside the frame while header and copyright stay put. Text obeys the same four columns; outer margins are 28px.

sections.description: The roster grid: four columns by many rows of identical square cells separated by 1px black lines, no gutters. Each cell centres a single glyph about 55% of the cell width, assembled from small black squares with hairline yellow gaps so the pixel grid shows, and a one-word caption in 14px mono centred near the bottom edge. Letters, symbols and tiny pictograms alternate without hierarchy, like a bitmap font specimen sheet.

Narrow screens get a full-bleed sky-blue lock-out card instead of the site: a two-line bitmap heading in near-black, centred slightly above the middle, with a seven-line centred mono paragraph beneath written in mock-military voice asking the visitor to return on a keyboard device. No navigation, no links, the same grain texture.

steal: Draw icons as pixels with visible gaps on the page's background colour, so the artwork and the ruled layout grid look like one system.
Set every word in one monospaced size and let weight and underlines carry the hierarchy, saving the bitmap face for a single button.
Let a strip of the next screen's contrasting colours peek in at one viewport edge to promise something behind the page.
